name: Zebul
overview: Zebul is a male figure known as the ruler of Shechem, as recorded in Judges 9:30. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, his leadership role in Shechem marks him as a notable figure within the biblical narrative. No additional personal notes are provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Zebul means 'elevation, height, lofty [temple],' reflecting a sense of prominence or exalted position. This proper name is noted in Judges 9:28 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Zebul as the lieutenant to Abimelech, indicating a position of authority and close association with this leader. Beyond this, there are no recorded family relationships for Zebul in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Zebul's significance lies in his role as the ruler of Shechem and his loyalty to Abimelech, serving as his lieutenant. His governance in Shechem during Abimelech's rule situates him within the political and military framework of the time, highlighting his part in the unfolding events recorded in Judges. Through this, Zebul contributes to the narrative of leadership and conflict in Israel's history.
